original_question: If a connected properly edge-colored n-regular graph satisfies the usual allowable-graph condition that every alternating i,j,i,j walk with |i-j| > 1 returns to its starting point, must it be the symmetry type graph of some maniplex?
target_in_paper: Section 1: the general realization problem stated as Conjecture 1.1, together with its two-vertex specialization/reformulation in Proposition 1.2 and the affirmative two-vertex result in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core realization problem: start from a connected, properly edge-coloured n-valent object satisfying the standard maniplex commutation/4-cycle condition for non-consecutive colors, and ask whether it can occur as the symmetry type graph of a maniplex.
missing_details: The paper works with n-premaniplexes (connected edge-coloured pregraphs), not just simple graphs; semi-edges are allowed and are essential in symmetry type graphs.
If the draft is meant to match the paper's main theorem, it must be restricted to the case of exactly two vertices, i.e. the symmetry type graph of a 2-orbit maniplex.
The colours are explicitly 0,1,...,n-1, and each vertex must be incident with exactly one edge or semi-edge of each colour.
The closure condition is stated as: whenever |i-j|>1, every alternating path of length 4 with colours i and j is closed.
The realization is as the symmetry type graph with respect to the full automorphism group of a rank-n maniplex.
The paper uses the canonical notation 2_I^n for the two-vertex n-premaniplexes; your draft omits this standard reformulation.

The paper's introductory conjecture is broader than your wording in one sense (all premaniplexes, not only simple graphs), but the main theorem is narrower in another sense (it proves only the two-vertex case).
The finiteness and connectedness assumptions on the premaniplex should be stated explicitly.
refined_question: Let X be a finite connected n-premaniplex with exactly two vertices; that is, X is a connected pregraph with edge/semiedge colours 0,1,...,n-1 such that each vertex is incident with exactly one edge or semi-edge of each colour and, whenever |i-j|>1, every alternating path of length 4 with colours i and j is closed. Must there exist a rank-n maniplex M whose symmetry type graph, with respect to its full automorphism group, is isomorphic to X?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every proper subset I of {0,1,...,n-1}, does there exist a 2-orbit rank-n maniplex whose symmetry type graph is 2_I^n, the two-vertex n-premaniplex having a semi-edge of colour i at each vertex for i in I and a colour-i edge joining the two vertices for i not in I?
justification: The introduction frames the general realization problem as whether every premaniplex can be realized as the symmetry type graph of a maniplex. The nearby introductory results then narrow to the two-vertex case: Proposition 1.2 gives the standard two-vertex reformulation, and Theorem 1.3 proves that every 2-vertex premaniplex is realizable. Your draft preserves the basic maniplex compatibility condition, but it is not fully paper-faithful because it speaks only about graphs rather than pregraphs/premaniplexes, does not allow semi-edges, and omits the crucial two-vertex restriction that is central to the theorem actually proved in the paper.
